rituals.vibeLine: Motivation was late, so we started without it.

rituals.predict: Guess whether the tiniest physical start changes motivation even one point.

rituals.mindBend: You may not need motivation to start; starting may be one way motivation gets made.

rituals.name: CROSS THE DOORWAY
rituals.title: CROSS THE DOORWAY
rituals.targetPattern: Decision paralysis before task contact
rituals.target_pattern: Decision paralysis before task contact
rituals.precise_subpattern: Decision paralysis before task contact
rituals.vibeLine: We tricked your body into arriving before your excuses.
rituals.hook: Move your body into the task zone before your brain holds another meeting.
rituals.predict: Guess whether crossing one physical boundary will make the task feel more real or more impossible.
rituals.play: Choose the doorway, desk, kitchen, car, shower or room connected to the task. Cross into that space and stop. You are allowed to do nothing else.
rituals.catch: Notice how the decision changes once your body has already changed context.
rituals.reveal: Physical context can cue action before motivation or certainty catches up.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes the first decision is not “do it.” It is “stand where doing it happens.”

Offer your brain a deal so small it suspects a scam.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Offer your brain a deal so small it suspects a scam.
Set two minutes. Work only until the timer. At the bell, stopping is genuinely allowed—even if momentum appears.
Guess whether starting for only two minutes feels less threatening than “finish it.”
Notice the difference between resistance to the whole task and resistance after two minutes of contact. The imagined size of a task often creates more friction than the first slice of the task.

rituals.name: STEAL FRICTION FROM TOMORROW
rituals.title: STEAL FRICTION FROM TOMORROW
rituals.targetPattern: Expecting later motivation to overcome same obstacles
rituals.target_pattern: Expecting later motivation to overcome same obstacles
rituals.precise_subpattern: Expecting later motivation to overcome same obstacles
rituals.vibeLine: Future-you just inherited fewer excuses.
rituals.hook: Do not do tomorrow’s task.
rituals.predict: Guess which tiny obstacle future-you is most likely to use as an excuse.
rituals.play: Remove exactly one friction point now: open the file, charge the device, put shoes by the door, place the form in the bag, fill the water bottle.
rituals.catch: Notice that the future task is objectively smaller without any future motivation being required.
rituals.reveal: Environment can carry part of the behavioural load that we usually dump onto willpower.
rituals.mindBend: Make tomorrow easier instead of demanding that tomorrow-you be stronger.

rituals.name: FIVE-SECOND CHOICE LOCK
rituals.title: FIVE-SECOND CHOICE LOCK
rituals.targetPattern: Reopening a reversible choice repeatedly
rituals.target_pattern: Reopening a reversible choice repeatedly
rituals.precise_subpattern: Reopening a reversible choice repeatedly
rituals.vibeLine: Five seconds. Pick a lane. You can change roads later.
rituals.hook: For one reversible choice, the parliament gets five seconds.
rituals.predict: Guess whether choosing quickly feels worse than continuing to hover.
rituals.play: Pick a low-stakes reversible decision. Count 5–4–3–2–1. At one, choose A or B and physically begin it. No reopening for 60 sec.
rituals.catch: Check if discomfort comes from the choice itself or from losing the option to keep deliberating.
rituals.reveal: Indecision can feel safer because every option remains imaginary and untested.
rituals.mindBend: A reversible choice rarely needs the emotional certainty of a permanent one.

rituals.name: UGLY FIRST BRICK
rituals.title: UGLY FIRST BRICK
rituals.targetPattern: Avoiding first attempt because quality feels diagnostic
rituals.target_pattern: Avoiding first attempt because quality feels diagnostic
rituals.precise_subpattern: Avoiding first attempt because quality feels diagnostic
rituals.vibeLine: We made it bad on purpose. Perfectionism has fewer weapons now.
rituals.hook: Make the first piece deliberately too ugly to judge you.
rituals.predict: Guess how bad you can allow the first thirty seconds to be.
rituals.play: Create the worst acceptable first fragment on purpose: one clumsy sentence, rough sketch, messy list, badly placed object. Label it “brick 1,” not “final.”
rituals.catch: Check if starting becomes easier when quality is no longer the entrance fee.
rituals.reveal: Perfectionism often protects identity by preventing visible imperfect attempts.
rituals.mindBend: A bad first brick is still more buildable than a perfect imaginary wall.

rituals.title: SHRINK RAY
rituals.targetPattern: Action represented at too large a grain size
rituals.target_pattern: Action represented at too large a grain size
rituals.precise_subpattern: Action represented at too large a grain size
rituals.vibeLine: We shrank the monster until it needed a microscope.
rituals.hook: Keep shrinking the task until resistance starts laughing.
rituals.predict: Guess the smallest version that feels almost too silly to count.
rituals.play: Take “do the task” and halve it repeatedly: finish report → write section → write paragraph → open file → type heading. Stop when the next step takes under fifteen seconds.
rituals.catch: Notice the exact size where “I can’t” becomes “well, obviously I can do that.”
rituals.reveal: Resistance is sensitive to task size, not only task importance.
rituals.mindBend: The first useful step can be embarrassingly small and still point in the right direction.

rituals.title: NINETY-SECOND EXIT
rituals.targetPattern: Belief a work session must complete the task
rituals.target_pattern: Belief a work session must complete the task
rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief a work session must complete the task
rituals.vibeLine: The task lost its “you live here now” clause.
rituals.hook: Start with the exit already guaranteed.
rituals.predict: Guess whether work feels safer when the timer—not completion—decides when you stop.
rituals.play: Set ninety seconds. Work on the task until the timer rings. At the bell, stop mid-progress on purpose. Leave one obvious next step visible.
rituals.catch: Check if starting felt easier when the session had a hard ending.
rituals.reveal: A bounded work period reduces the hidden fear that starting means being trapped until completion.
rituals.mindBend: You can enter a task more easily when the exit door is visible.

VIBE: UNFILTERED

Starting is easier when you know exactly when you can get the hell out.

HOOK
Start with the exit already guaranteed.

PREDICT
Guess whether work feels safer when the timer—not completion—decides when you stop.

PLAY
Set ninety seconds. Work on the task until the timer rings. At the bell, stop mid-progress on purpose. Leave one obvious next step visible.

CATCH
Check if starting felt easier when the session had a hard ending.

REVEAL
A bounded work period reduces the hidden fear that starting means being trapped until completion.

MIND BEND
You can enter a task more easily when the exit door is visible.

MOVE ON

rituals.vibeLine: We fired most of the menu for one minute.

rituals.predict: Guess whether losing options feels relieving or irritating.

rituals.mindBend: Sometimes freedom returns when you temporarily close a few doors.

rituals.name: BORROW MOMENTUM
rituals.title: BORROW MOMENTUM
rituals.targetPattern: New action lacking a reliable cue
rituals.target_pattern: New action lacking a reliable cue
rituals.precise_subpattern: New action lacking a reliable cue
rituals.vibeLine: Why start a new engine when one is already moving?
rituals.hook: Attach the new action to something already guaranteed to happen.
rituals.predict: Guess which existing event is most reliable today: kettle, shower, login, lunch, getting home, brushing teeth.
rituals.play: Choose one routine event. Add a ten-second action immediately after it: “After I close the shower door, I put medicine by the kettle.” Say the pair once as a single sentence.
rituals.catch: Notice how much easier the action is to picture when the cue is already alive.
rituals.reveal: Existing routines can carry new behaviour like a moving walkway.
rituals.mindBend: Do not build every habit from zero. Borrow a cue that already knows how to show up.

rituals.name: PROCRASTINATION COSTUME
rituals.title: PROCRASTINATION COSTUME
rituals.targetPattern: Task avoidance hiding emotion avoidance
rituals.target_pattern: Task avoidance hiding emotion avoidance
rituals.precise_subpattern: Task avoidance hiding emotion avoidance
rituals.vibeLine: The task took off the mask. Underneath: one annoying feeling.
rituals.hook: The task may not be the thing you are avoiding.
rituals.predict: Guess which feeling is hiding underneath: boredom, confusion, shame, uncertainty, resentment, fear of failure, fear of success.
rituals.play: Name the task. Complete: “If I started right now, the feeling I least want is ____.” Then choose a first step that allows that feeling to be present rather than trying to remove it first.
rituals.catch: Check if the task becomes clearer once the hidden emotion gets named.
rituals.reveal: Procrastination often regulates emotion in the short term rather than time in the long term.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes you are not avoiding the task. You are avoiding the feeling attached to the first minute.

rituals.name: TOUCH THE TOOL
rituals.title: TOUCH THE TOOL
rituals.targetPattern: Task remains abstract until contact with a tool
rituals.target_pattern: Task remains abstract until contact with a tool
rituals.precise_subpattern: Task remains abstract until contact with a tool
rituals.vibeLine: The task is now annoyingly real.
rituals.hook: No productivity. Physical contact.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the task feels different after you touch the first object required for it.
rituals.play: Pick up the pen, open the laptop, hold the gym shoes, grab the washing basket—whatever tool belongs to the task. Do nothing else for five seconds.
rituals.catch: Check if the task becomes more concrete once your body is in contact with its first object.
rituals.reveal: Abstract tasks carry more friction than physically instantiated ones.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes motivation starts with an object, not an emotion.

Apparently your brain works better when the buffet is covered.

HOOK
Your brain has twelve tabs open.

PREDICT
Guess which task you would choose if every other option were temporarily hidden.

PLAY
Pick 1 action. Physically hide the others: close tabs, turn over the list, move items out of sight, or cover everything below the first line.

CATCH
Check if indecision changes when competing cues disappear.

REVEAL
Choice overload is partly created by simultaneous visibility.

MIND BEND
You do not need fewer responsibilities forever. You may need fewer of them in the visual field right now.

rituals.name: COIN FLINCH
rituals.title: COIN FLINCH
rituals.targetPattern: Indecision hiding a latent preference
rituals.target_pattern: Indecision hiding a latent preference
rituals.precise_subpattern: Indecision hiding a latent preference
rituals.vibeLine: Heads said A. Your face said “ugh.” Useful.
rituals.hook: The coin is not deciding.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you secretly prefer one option before the coin lands.

rituals.catch: Use the reaction as information—not as a command.
rituals.reveal: Randomness can reveal preference by removing the burden of choosing for one second.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes you discover what you want when chance pretends to choose for you.

rituals.name: ENERGY LANE
rituals.title: ENERGY LANE
rituals.targetPattern: Choosing tasks as if capacity were constant
rituals.target_pattern: Choosing tasks as if capacity were constant
rituals.precise_subpattern: Choosing tasks as if capacity were constant
rituals.vibeLine: Maybe stop scheduling 4K rendering on 12% battery.
rituals.hook: Stop asking low-battery you to run the high-performance app.
rituals.predict: Guess your current usable energy: low, medium or high.
rituals.play: Choose a task version that matches the lane. LOW: prepare or reduce friction. MEDIUM: do one chunk. HIGH: tackle the hard section. No moral ranking between lanes.
rituals.catch: Check if action becomes easier when capacity and demand match.
rituals.reveal: Planning works better when it includes the state of the system doing the work.
rituals.mindBend: Low energy is a planning variable, not a character diagnosis.

rituals.vibeLine: Your brain likes same-day shipping on rewards.
rituals.hook: We are moving the reward closer, not making the task prettier.
rituals.predict: Guess whether a tiny reward after the first step changes willingness more than a big reward after completion.
rituals.play: Choose one immediate, harmless reward—song, tea, stretch, funny clip. Make it available only after the first concrete step, not after the whole task.
rituals.catch: Check if the task now has a nearer payoff.
rituals.reveal: Distant rewards lose motivational power compared with immediate ones.
rituals.mindBend: Your brain discounts faraway prizes. Bring one closer to the start line.

VIBE: UNFILTERED

Stop making motivation wait until the damn project is over.

HOOK
We are moving the reward closer, not making the task prettier.

PREDICT
Guess whether a tiny reward after the first step changes willingness more than a big reward after completion.

PLAY
Choose one immediate, harmless reward—song, tea, stretch, funny clip. Make it available only after the first concrete step, not after the whole task.

CATCH
Check if the task now has a nearer payoff.

REVEAL
Distant rewards lose motivational power compared with immediate ones.

MIND BEND
Your brain discounts faraway prizes. Bring one closer to the start line.

MOVE ON

rituals.name: LEAVE A BREADCRUMB
rituals.title: LEAVE A BREADCRUMB
rituals.targetPattern: Pausing without a re-entry cue
rituals.target_pattern: Pausing without a re-entry cue
rituals.precise_subpattern: Pausing without a re-entry cue
rituals.vibeLine: Kind of you not to abandon tomorrow-you in the wilderness.
rituals.hook: Future-you hates reopening a task with no clue where to start.
rituals.predict: Guess whether tomorrow’s restart feels easier if you leave one obvious re-entry instruction.
rituals.play: Before stopping a task, write one line: “NEXT: ___.” Make it painfully concrete—open section 3, call Alex, add total, wash pan.
rituals.catch: Imagine returning with no memory of today’s context and test whether the line is enough.
rituals.reveal: Stopping becomes expensive when future-you has to reconstruct the whole mental state.
rituals.mindBend: A good stopping point contains the start of the next session.

rituals.vibeLine: Motivation can catch up; your shoes already voted.

rituals.mindBend: Sometimes the first decision is not “do it.” It is “stand where doing happens.”

rituals.name: RESTART TAX
rituals.title: RESTART TAX
rituals.targetPattern: Immediate relief masking repeated restart cost
rituals.target_pattern: Immediate relief masking repeated restart cost
rituals.precise_subpattern: Immediate relief masking repeated restart cost
rituals.vibeLine: Escape is allowed. Abandoning clues is optional.
rituals.hook: Avoiding feels cheap because the bill arrives later.
rituals.predict: Guess how many minutes tomorrow will be spent merely remembering where you left off if you stop now.
rituals.play: Before escaping, spend 20 sec creating a restart package: save, label, place materials, write next step. You may stop.
rituals.catch: Compare the relief of stopping with and without the restart package.
rituals.reveal: Avoidance has a hidden future cost: re-entry.
rituals.mindBend: You can stop without making tomorrow pay full price.

rituals.name: PAIR THE BORING
rituals.title: PAIR THE BORING
rituals.targetPattern: An aversive task lacking immediate pleasure
rituals.target_pattern: An aversive task lacking immediate pleasure
rituals.precise_subpattern: An aversive task lacking immediate pleasure
rituals.vibeLine: Spreadsheet, meet favourite playlist.
rituals.hook: Give the boring thing a harmless passenger.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the task feels less aversive when paired with something you already enjoy.
rituals.play: Choose one pleasure that can safely coexist with the task—music, favourite drink, podcast, comfy location. Reserve it for the task window.
rituals.catch: Check if the task acquires a new cue or pull.
rituals.reveal: Pairing immediate enjoyment with delayed-benefit behaviour can change approach motivation.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to make the task fun. You can stop making it travel alone.

rituals.name: DRAW THE FINISH LINE FIRST
rituals.title: DRAW THE FINISH LINE FIRST
rituals.targetPattern: Tasks feeling endless because ‘done’ is undefined
rituals.target_pattern: Tasks feeling endless because ‘done’ is undefined
rituals.precise_subpattern: Tasks feeling endless because ‘done’ is undefined
rituals.vibeLine: Turns out “forever” was a terrible task duration.
rituals.hook: Do not start until you know where stopping is allowed.
rituals.predict: Guess how long the task feels when “done” has no visible boundary.
rituals.play: Define today’s finish line before touching the task: one page, ten items, twenty minutes, one call, clear one surface. Make it smaller than the whole project.
rituals.catch: Check if beginning feels safer when stopping is permitted and specific.
rituals.reveal: Endless tasks create avoidance because the brain cannot price the commitment.
rituals.mindBend: A visible finish line makes starting a bounded decision.

rituals.targetPattern: Task delay protecting against a predicted feeling
rituals.target_pattern: Task delay protecting against a predicted feeling
rituals.precise_subpattern: Task delay protecting against a predicted feeling
rituals.vibeLine: Ah. We were avoiding confusion, not the email.
rituals.hook: Maybe the task is not the scary part.
rituals.predict: Guess which feeling appears first if you imagine starting: boredom, confusion, shame, frustration, uncertainty, effort, fear of being judged.
rituals.play: Name only the feeling. Choose an action small enough to contact the task for 10 sec while allowing that feeling to come along.
rituals.catch: See whether the emotion is survivable at micro-dose size.
rituals.reveal: Avoidance often targets an internal experience rather than the external task itself.
rituals.mindBend: You may not need to love the task; you may only need to make room for the first feeling it triggers.

rituals.name: LEAVE IT IN THE PATH
rituals.title: LEAVE IT IN THE PATH
rituals.targetPattern: A future task forgotten because the environment gives no prompt
rituals.target_pattern: A future task forgotten because the environment gives no prompt
rituals.precise_subpattern: A future task forgotten because the environment gives no prompt
rituals.vibeLine: Your floor may be more reliable than your memory.
rituals.hook: Memory is optional when the environment can remind you.
rituals.predict: Guess where your body will definitely pass before the action matters.
rituals.play: Place a safe cue in that path: bag by door, form on keyboard, bottle beside keys, note on shoes. Don’t rely on remembering.
rituals.catch: Notice how the future reminder becomes physical.
rituals.reveal: Prospective memory improves when cues appear at the moment of action.
rituals.mindBend: The environment can remember on your behalf.

cheeky.play: Place a safe cue in that path: bag by door, form on keyboard, bottle beside keys, note on shoes. Don’t rely on remembering.
cheeky.catch: Notice how the future reminder becomes physical.
cheeky.reveal: Prospective memory improves when cues appear at the moment of action.
cheeky.mindBend: The environment can remember on your behalf.
cheeky.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: BORROW A WITNESS
rituals.title: BORROW A WITNESS
rituals.targetPattern: Task initiation improved by perceived co-presence
rituals.target_pattern: Task initiation improved by perceived co-presence
rituals.precise_subpattern: Task initiation improved by perceived co-presence
rituals.vibeLine: No coaching. Just somebody existing near the start line.
rituals.hook: Some tasks start easier when another human exists nearby.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you would begin faster if someone silently watched you start.
rituals.play: Imagine a trusted person sitting nearby for 60 sec, or use a real body-doubling setup if available. Your only job is to begin one visible action.
rituals.catch: Check if imagined or actual co-presence changes activation.
rituals.reveal: Human presence can alter arousal and task engagement even without help.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes you do not need advice. You need a witness to the first move.

rituals.title: TOMORROW’S FIRST MINUTE
rituals.targetPattern: Future benefit too abstract to motivate present effort
rituals.target_pattern: Future benefit too abstract to motivate present effort
rituals.precise_subpattern: Future benefit too abstract to motivate present effort
rituals.vibeLine: Tomorrow became less theoretical.
rituals.hook: Do not picture the whole future benefit.
rituals.predict: Guess the first tiny inconvenience future-you avoids if you act now.
rituals.play: Imagine tomorrow at the exact moment the benefit arrives: clean mug ready, email already sent, bag packed, document started. Describe only that first relieved minute.
rituals.catch: Check if the reward becomes more concrete.
rituals.reveal: Near, specific consequences motivate differently from vague future benefits.
rituals.mindBend: Future-you becomes easier to care about when they have a scene, not a slogan.

rituals.name: BETWEEN TWO THINGS
rituals.title: BETWEEN TWO THINGS
rituals.targetPattern: New behaviour lacking a stable sequence position
rituals.target_pattern: New behaviour lacking a stable sequence position
rituals.precise_subpattern: New behaviour lacking a stable sequence position
rituals.vibeLine: Floating task finally got assigned a seat.
rituals.hook: Your new habit needs neighbours.
rituals.predict: Guess which two existing routines could sandwich it.
rituals.play: Choose an action that already happens before and one that happens after. Place the new behaviour between them: coffee → medication → shower, for example.
rituals.catch: Notice how the habit gains a fixed slot instead of floating in the day.
rituals.reveal: Sequences are easier to retrieve when actions have stable neighbours.
rituals.mindBend: A habit sticks better when it knows who comes before and after.

rituals.name: MAKE GOOD EASY TO SEE
rituals.title: MAKE GOOD EASY TO SEE
rituals.targetPattern: Desired behaviour stored out of sight
rituals.target_pattern: Desired behaviour stored out of sight
rituals.precise_subpattern: Desired behaviour stored out of sight
rituals.vibeLine: Good behaviour gets shelf placement too.
rituals.hook: Out of sight is doing more behavioural engineering than you think.
rituals.predict: Guess which helpful action would happen more if its cue were visible.
rituals.play: Move one benign helpful object into easy view: water bottle, book, walking shoes, fruit, notebook. Change nothing else.
rituals.catch: Notice how visibility changes the number of moments the behaviour gets remembered.
rituals.reveal: What is visible gets more opportunities to compete for action.
rituals.mindBend: Environment design can create reminders without nagging you.

rituals.name: HANDOFF NOTE
rituals.title: HANDOFF NOTE
rituals.targetPattern: Starting blocked by lingering cognitive residue from prior task
rituals.target_pattern: Starting blocked by lingering cognitive residue from prior task
rituals.precise_subpattern: Starting blocked by lingering cognitive residue from prior task
rituals.vibeLine: Your last task was ghosting the new one.
rituals.hook: Part of your brain may still be in the previous task.
rituals.predict: Guess the one unfinished sentence your last activity is still holding.
rituals.play: Before switching, write one closure line for the previous task: “Stopped at ___; next is ___.” Then physically close or minimise it before opening the new one.
rituals.catch: Check if the new task gets cleaner attention.
rituals.reveal: Unfinished task residue can follow you across switches.
rituals.mindBend: A clean handoff is easier than dragging two workspaces through one doorway.

rituals.name: STOPPING CAN SAVE THE REST
rituals.title: STOPPING CAN SAVE THE REST
rituals.targetPattern: Continuing because stopping would make past effort feel wasted
rituals.target_pattern: Continuing because stopping would make past effort feel wasted
rituals.precise_subpattern: Continuing because stopping would make past effort feel wasted
rituals.vibeLine: You cannot rescue yesterday by sacrificing tomorrow.
rituals.hook: Past effort is gone.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you would continue if you had only five minutes invested so far.
rituals.play: Pretend the past effort cost is zero. Look only at the next block of time or money. Is continuing still the best use of it?
rituals.catch: Check if the answer changes when sunk effort loses voting rights.
rituals.reveal: Past costs cannot be recovered by spending more.
rituals.mindBend: Stopping does not waste the past. It protects the future from joining it.

rituals.mindBend: Not every choice deserves fresh creativity.

rituals.targetPattern: Many important tasks making none behaviourally dominant
rituals.target_pattern: Many important tasks making none behaviourally dominant
rituals.precise_subpattern: Many important tasks making none behaviourally dominant
rituals.vibeLine: Everything may matter. Only one thing gets the chair.

rituals.predict: Guess which task you would choose if “importance” were banned and only “next” mattered.

rituals.mindBend: You do not need one true priority for life. You need one next move.

rituals.name: GIVE THE OBSTACLE A SCRIPT
rituals.title: GIVE THE OBSTACLE A SCRIPT
rituals.targetPattern: Known obstacle repeatedly derailing action
rituals.target_pattern: Known obstacle repeatedly derailing action
rituals.precise_subpattern: Known obstacle repeatedly derailing action
rituals.vibeLine: Your plan now includes the annoying part where life happens.
rituals.hook: Your plan has a hero.
rituals.predict: Guess the first predictable thing that usually knocks this action off course.
rituals.play: Finish two sentences: “If ___ happens, then instead of quitting I will ___.” Keep the fallback smaller than the original plan.
rituals.catch: Notice how the obstacle becomes part of the plan rather than evidence the plan failed.
rituals.reveal: Plans are more robust when predictable friction has a pre-decided response.
rituals.mindBend: An obstacle is less powerful when it stops being a surprise.

rituals.targetPattern: Open-ended work expanding because stopping is undefined
rituals.target_pattern: Open-ended work expanding because stopping is undefined
rituals.precise_subpattern: Open-ended work expanding because stopping is undefined
rituals.vibeLine: Important does not mean all-day tenancy.
rituals.hook: The task is trying to occupy the whole day because nobody gave it walls.
rituals.predict: Guess how long you can work usefully before quality drops.
rituals.play: Choose a start time and stop time first. Make the box smaller than your fear of the task. Work only inside that box.
rituals.catch: Check if a bounded container changes resistance.
rituals.reveal: Open-ended effort is hard to price; bounded effort is easier to choose.
rituals.mindBend: A task can be important without being allowed to eat the day.

VIBE: UNFILTERED

Put the damn task in a damn box before it eats the calendar.

HOOK
The task is trying to occupy the whole day because nobody gave it walls.

PREDICT
Guess how long you can work usefully before quality drops.

PLAY
Choose a start time and stop time first. Make the box smaller than your fear of the task. Work only inside that box.

CATCH
Check if a bounded container changes resistance.

REVEAL
Open-ended effort is hard to price; bounded effort is easier to choose.

MIND BEND
A task can be important without being allowed to eat the day.

MOVE ON
↻ PUT IT IN A BOX

rituals.name: HALF THE CONTAINER
rituals.title: HALF THE CONTAINER
rituals.targetPattern: Work expanding to fill available time
rituals.target_pattern: Work expanding to fill available time
rituals.precise_subpattern: Work expanding to fill available time
rituals.vibeLine: Interesting how the decorative procrastination did not fit.
rituals.hook: A giant time window can turn a small task into fog.
rituals.predict: Guess what would happen if you had half as long as usual.
rituals.play: Take a routine task you know reasonably well. Give it a realistic but tighter window—about half the casual buffer, not half the necessary work.
rituals.catch: Notice which low-value behaviours disappear first.
rituals.reveal: Available time shapes how much process accumulates around a task.
rituals.mindBend: More time can create more work without creating more value.

rituals.name: DISTRACTION CAN WAIT TEN
rituals.title: DISTRACTION CAN WAIT TEN
rituals.targetPattern: Immediate distraction winning before long-term goal can compete
rituals.target_pattern: Immediate distraction winning before long-term goal can compete
rituals.precise_subpattern: Immediate distraction winning before long-term goal can compete
rituals.vibeLine: Not banned. Just asked to wait in reception.
rituals.hook: You do not have to defeat the distraction.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the urge will still feel equally urgent in ten minutes.
rituals.play: When the distraction appears, schedule it for ten minutes later instead of banning it. Put the exact time somewhere visible.
rituals.catch: Check if 'later' creates less rebellion than 'never.'
rituals.reveal: Short delays can weaken impulsive choice without demanding permanent denial.
rituals.mindBend: An urge can be postponed without becoming a moral battle.
rituals.ritualCard:

rituals.target_pattern: Abstract motivation ignoring the actual friction point

rituals.vibeLine: Turns out 'lazy' was hiding behind a missing password.
rituals.hook: Stop calling the task hard.
rituals.predict: Guess which part of the first minute creates the most delay.

rituals.name: THE NOT-DOING LIST
rituals.title: THE NOT-DOING LIST
rituals.targetPattern: Overcommitment maintained because stopping is never planned
rituals.target_pattern: Overcommitment maintained because stopping is never planned
rituals.precise_subpattern: Overcommitment maintained because stopping is never planned
rituals.vibeLine: Amazing how the schedule improves when something actually leaves.
rituals.hook: Your plan may need an empty chair more than another task.
rituals.predict: Guess which low-value action is most likely to steal the time you need.
rituals.play: Choose one thing you will deliberately not do during the work window: inbox, social feed, optional errand, perfect formatting, unnecessary research.
rituals.catch: Notice how a negative boundary can protect a positive action.
rituals.reveal: Capacity is created by exclusion as well as motivation.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes productivity is deciding what does not get a turn.
rituals.ritualCard:
Your plan may need an empty chair more than another task.

Notice how a negative boundary can protect a positive action. Capacity is created by exclusion as well as motivation.

rituals.name: IT FAILED. WHY?
rituals.title: IT FAILED. WHY?
rituals.targetPattern: Imagining failure exposing preventable risks before action
rituals.target_pattern: Imagining failure exposing preventable risks before action
rituals.precise_subpattern: Imagining failure exposing preventable risks before action
rituals.vibeLine: Congratulations, the disaster happened only in rehearsal.
rituals.hook: Pretend the plan already failed.
rituals.predict: Guess the most boring reason the plan would fail—not the dramatic one.
rituals.play: Imagine it is one week later and the attempt failed. List three reasons, then circle the one you can prevent before starting.
rituals.catch: Notice how risks become easier to see after pretending the outcome is already known.
rituals.reveal: Prospective hindsight can surface obstacles optimism skips.
rituals.mindBend: Failure imagined early can be cheaper than failure explained late.

rituals.vibeLine: Not now finally stopped sounding like never.

rituals.name: BORROW A HUMAN SHADOW
rituals.title: BORROW A HUMAN SHADOW
rituals.targetPattern: Another person's quiet presence supporting task initiation
rituals.target_pattern: Another person's quiet presence supporting task initiation
rituals.precise_subpattern: Another person's quiet presence supporting task initiation
rituals.vibeLine: No coaching. Just another mammal doing tasks.
rituals.hook: Sometimes focus improves when another person is simply existing nearby.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you would start faster with someone quietly working beside you.
rituals.play: Use a safe low-pressure body double: work beside someone, join a silent study room, or keep a trusted person on a quiet call while both do separate tasks.
rituals.catch: Check if initiation or staying changes even without reminders.
rituals.reveal: Social presence can provide external structure and attentional anchoring.
rituals.mindBend: Support does not always need advice; sometimes it just needs another chair.

rituals.vibeLine: Apparently your brain protects badges like family heirlooms.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Alternating related skill types improving discrimination despite feeling harder
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain lost autopilot and gained actual choosing.
rituals.hook: Easy practice can feel better while teaching less.
rituals.predict: Guess which feels smoother: doing ten identical examples or mixing three related types.

rituals.catch: Check if practice feels harder because you must identify the right method each time.

rituals.mindBend: Harder practice can be better learning.

rituals.name: GUESS BEFORE YOU LOOK
rituals.title: GUESS BEFORE YOU LOOK
rituals.targetPattern: Producing an answer before seeing it improving learning
rituals.target_pattern: Producing an answer before seeing it improving learning
rituals.precise_subpattern: Producing an answer before seeing it improving learning
rituals.vibeLine: Being wrong for five seconds can help you learn the right thing.
rituals.hook: Your wrong guess can teach more than immediate reading.
rituals.predict: Guess the answer before opening the note, solution, definition, or instructions.
rituals.play: Give yourself five seconds to generate an answer—even incomplete—then reveal the real one and compare.
rituals.catch: Notice how the difference becomes unusually memorable.
rituals.reveal: Information is often remembered better when first generated rather than only read.
rituals.mindBend: A failed guess can create a hook for the correct answer.

rituals.vibeLine: Ten seconds just got an annual budget review.
rituals.hook: A task can be cheap once and expensive one hundred times.
rituals.predict: Guess which repeated ten-second hassle appears every time you do the behaviour.
rituals.play: Find one recurring micro-tax: password, cable, missing file, shoes upstairs, messy surface, unclear template. Remove it once.
rituals.catch: Notice the difference between motivation work and infrastructure work.
rituals.reveal: Small repeated frictions compound across repetitions.
rituals.mindBend: A ten-second tax paid daily can shape behaviour more than a motivational speech.

rituals.title: LEAVE TOMORROW FEWER DOORS
rituals.targetPattern: Future choice narrowed in advance to protect a goal
rituals.target_pattern: Future choice narrowed in advance to protect a goal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Future choice narrowed in advance to protect a goal
rituals.vibeLine: Fewer doors, fewer negotiations.
rituals.hook: Tomorrow-you may not need more discipline.
rituals.predict: Guess which tempting alternative will be easiest to choose later.
rituals.play: Change one environment now: pack lunch, leave card at home, block site, place gym clothes out, prebook transport, remove app from home screen.
rituals.catch: Notice how future choice becomes structurally simpler.
rituals.reveal: Commitment devices protect intentions by changing later option availability or friction.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes freedom now can buy freedom from negotiation later.

rituals.name: CHECKMARKS CAN LIE
rituals.title: CHECKMARKS CAN LIE

rituals.predict: Guess which tiny task you want to do mostly because it gives a fast checkmark.

rituals.catch: Notice how checkmark hunger competes with real progress.
rituals.reveal: Completion itself is rewarding, which can bias task selection.
rituals.mindBend: A finished trivial task is still trivial.

rituals.name: EARLY-BUCKET EFFECT
rituals.title: EARLY-BUCKET EFFECT
rituals.targetPattern: Doing tasks too early to clear mental load despite extra effort
rituals.target_pattern: Doing tasks too early to clear mental load despite extra effort
rituals.precise_subpattern: Doing tasks too early to clear mental load despite extra effort
rituals.vibeLine: You may be carrying the bucket early just to stop seeing it.
rituals.hook: Sometimes we rush to finish to stop thinking about the task.
rituals.predict: Guess whether doing it now is actually efficient—or merely relieving.
rituals.play: Take the urge to complete something early. Compare effort now versus effort at the natural time. Include carrying, rework, waiting, double handling.
rituals.catch: Check if mental relief is worth the practical cost.
rituals.reveal: People sometimes act early to reduce cognitive load even when it increases physical effort.
rituals.mindBend: Sooner can feel cleaner without being smarter.

jolly.catch: Check if mental relief is worth the practical cost.
jolly.reveal: People sometimes act early to reduce cognitive load even when it increases physical effort.
jolly.mindBend: Sooner can feel cleaner without being smarter.
jolly.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: GIVE FUN AN ENDING TOO
rituals.targetPattern: Leisure leaking into avoidance because it has no boundary
rituals.target_pattern: Leisure leaking into avoidance because it has no boundary
rituals.precise_subpattern: Leisure leaking into avoidance because it has no boundary
rituals.vibeLine: Enjoy it properly, then leave when the episode ends.
rituals.hook: A break without an ending can quietly become the evening.
rituals.predict: Guess what cue will end the leisure period.
rituals.play: Before starting the fun thing, choose an exit cue: one episode, one game, 20 minutes, when tea is finished, after this chapter.
rituals.catch: Check if leisure feels safer when it has an intentional container.
rituals.reveal: Enjoyment becomes easier to regulate when stopping is specified in advance.
rituals.mindBend: A boundary can protect fun from becoming guilt.

rituals.vibeLine: No lifetime membership required.
rituals.hook: Your brain is refusing the whole mountain.

rituals.reveal: Short commitments preserve autonomy while enabling contact with the task.
rituals.mindBend: You can commit to now without committing to forever.

rituals.name: MAKE THE BAD PATH ANNOYING
rituals.title: MAKE THE BAD PATH ANNOYING
rituals.targetPattern: Unwanted behaviour reduced by making it slightly less convenient
rituals.target_pattern: Unwanted behaviour reduced by making it slightly less convenient
rituals.precise_subpattern: Unwanted behaviour reduced by making it slightly less convenient
rituals.vibeLine: Not banned. Just mildly bureaucratic.
rituals.hook: You do not need to ban the habit.
rituals.predict: Guess one extra step that would interrupt autopilot without creating a crisis.
rituals.play: Add friction: store snacks out of reach, unplug device, use website blocker, move remote, require a password, keep card elsewhere.
rituals.catch: Check if a tiny cost creates a conscious choice.
rituals.reveal: Behaviour frequency is sensitive to small response costs.
rituals.mindBend: Mild inconvenience can do work that willpower keeps getting blamed for.

rituals.vibeLine: Same work, fewer hostage vibes.

rituals.reveal: Partitioning commitments can reduce perceived burden and preserve autonomy.

rituals.title: STOP RE-DECIDING AFTER THE DECISION
rituals.targetPattern: Continuing to deliberate after a decision has been made weakening implementation
rituals.target_pattern: Continuing to deliberate after a decision has been made weakening implementation
rituals.precise_subpattern: Continuing to deliberate after a decision has been made weakening implementation
rituals.vibeLine: Decision signed. Stop reopening the tender.
rituals.hook: Your decision may be done while your brain keeps reopening the committee meeting.
rituals.predict: Guess which question belongs before the choice and which belongs after it.
rituals.play: Take a reversible low-stakes decision already made. Put remaining thoughts into PRE-DECISION or IMPLEMENTATION. Only act on implementation questions now.
rituals.catch: Notice how option comparison keeps pulling attention backward.
rituals.reveal: Decision-making and implementation benefit from different mindsets.
rituals.mindBend: After crossing the decision line, more comparison can become friction rather than wisdom.

rituals.vibeLine: One word—'now'—just rewrote the contract.

rituals.mindBend: Your values may not have changed; the clock moved one reward into the gravitational field of now.
